# Indie Hackers Revenue, Products & Founder Stories Scraper

Indie Hackers is a public directory of bootstrapped products and the founders behind them. This actor reads the cookieless HTML the site serves today and returns product records with revenue, month-by-month revenue history, founders, screenshots, built-with tools and related products, plus the filterable founder case-study database.

No account, cookie, API key or proxy configuration is required. The site's public pages are fetched with a browser-compatible TLS profile, and every field comes from what the page actually shows.

## Modes

| Mode | What it returns |
| --- | --- |
| `products` | Product records from the product database, including monthly revenue and optional Stripe revenue history. Supports product keyword, category, business model, audience, revenue range and Stripe-verified filters, sorting, and pagination. |
| `interviews` | Founder case studies from the case-study database. Supports keyword, industry, learnings, business-model, revenue, employee-count and location filters, four sort orders, and pagination. |
| `byUrl` | Resolves exact `/product/<slug>` and `/post/<id>` URLs (old `/interview/<id>` links are mapped too). |

## Input

| Field | Used in | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | all | `products` | `products`, `interviews` or `byUrl`. The old `groups` value is still accepted and explains that Indie Hackers removed groups. |
| `searchQuery` | products | – | Keyword match on product name, tagline, category and audience. |
| `sortBy` | products | `revenue-desc` | `revenue-desc` (default), `verified-revenue` (the site's default order), `revenue-asc` or `name-asc`. Legacy `foundedDate-desc` and `memberCount-desc` are accepted and mapped to the closest supported order. |
| `productType` | products | Any product type | One directory category, e.g. Software, Newsletter, Marketplace. |
| `businessModel` | products | Any business model | One of the site's eight directory business models. |
| `audience` | products | Any audience | One of the directory's "Built for" audiences. |
| `minRevenue` | products | – | Minimum monthly revenue in USD. |
| `maxRevenue` | products | – | Maximum monthly revenue in USD. |
| `verifiedRevenueOnly` | products | `false` | Keep only Stripe-verified revenue. |
| `includeRevenueHistory` | products | `true` | Include the full month-by-month revenue series (no extra request). |
| `interviewSortBy` | interviews | `newest` | `newest` (default), `oldest`, `highest-revenue` or `lowest-revenue`. |
| `interviewKeyword` | interviews | – | Match story title, founder or company. |
| `interviewIndustries` | interviews | – | One or more industry tags (OR within this filter). |
| `interviewLearnings` | interviews | – | One or more learning tags. |
| `interviewBusinessModels` | interviews | – | One or more business-model tags. |
| `interviewMinRevenue` | interviews | – | Minimum company monthly revenue in USD. |
| `interviewMaxRevenue` | interviews | – | Maximum company monthly revenue in USD. |
| `interviewMinEmployees` | interviews | – | Minimum company size. |
| `interviewMaxEmployees` | interviews | – | Maximum company size. |
| `interviewLocation` | interviews | – | Word-prefix match on the founder's city/region/country, e.g. `new york` or `berlin`. |
| `includeInterviewDetails` | interviews | `false` | Open each selected story for article text, author, summary and image. |
| `pageUrls` | byUrl | – | Product or story URLs to resolve. |
| `maxItems` | all | `50` | Maximum records after filtering (1–500). |
| `offset` | all | `0` | Skip the first N results after sorting; use with `maxItems` to page. |

### Example: top products by revenue, with history

```json
{
  "mode": "products",
  "sortBy": "revenue-desc",
  "minRevenue": 10000,
  "maxItems": 25,
  "includeRevenueHistory": true
}
```

### Example: high-revenue SaaS case studies

```json
{
  "mode": "interviews",
  "interviewSortBy": "highest-revenue",
  "interviewIndustries": ["Software", "Developer Tools"],
  "interviewMinRevenue": 10000,
  "maxItems": 20
}
```

### Example: exact URLs

```json
{
  "mode": "byUrl",
  "pageUrls": [
    "https://www.indiehackers.com/product/ghost",
    "https://www.indiehackers.com/post/B1qKroz4HFqqH47eGHTD"
  ]
}
```

## Product output

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `recordType` | `product`. |
| `name`, `slug`, `tagline` | Product identity and one-line description. |
| `websiteUrl`, `indiehackersUrl`, `logoUrl` | Product website, profile page and logo. |
| `monthlyRevenue` | Latest reported monthly revenue in USD. |
| `revenueVerified` | `true` when the figure is Stripe-verified. |
| `revenueSource`, `revenueLabel`, `revenueCurrency` | Where the figure comes from and which period it covers. |
| `revenueHistory` | `[{ "month": "2026-10", "revenue": 911000 }]` when the product publishes a monthly series. |
| `launchDate` | First reported month (`YYYY-MM`). |
| `productType`, `whatItDoes`, `audienceKinds`, `audienceGroups` | Directory categories, jobs-to-be-done and audience. |
| `platforms`, `businessModel`, `revenueModel` | Platform list and business-model tags. |
| `twitterHandle`, `twitterUrl`, `facebookUrl`, `githubHandle`, `githubUrl` | Social profiles the product lists. |
| `founderCount`, `founders` | Founder count and `[{ username, name, role, bio, since, twitterHandle, avatarUrl }]`. |
| `founderUsername`, `founderName`, `founderAvatarUrl` | First founder, kept for older integrations. |
| `screenshots` | Product screenshots with page URL, caption and capture date. |
| `builtWith` | Tools detected on the product's website, with category. |
| `similarProducts` | Related products shown on the profile. |
| `scrapedAt` | ISO timestamp. |

## Case-study output

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `recordType` | `interview`. |
| `title`, `slug`, `interviewUrl` | Story title, post ID and absolute URL. |
| `intervieweeName`, `companyName` | Founder and company shown in the database card. |
| `monthlyRevenue` | Company monthly revenue reported in the database. |
| `employeeCount`, `location` | Company size and founder location. |
| `industries`, `learnings`, `businessModels` | The same tags the site's filters use. |
| `publishedDate`, `createdDate` | ISO publication date. |
| `authorName`, `authorUrl`, `summary`, `imageUrl`, `articleText`, `wordCount` | Added when `includeInterviewDetails` is on. |
| `scrapedAt` | ISO timestamp. |

## FAQ

**Do I need cookies or a proxy?** No. The actor reads the public pages with a browser TLS fingerprint and no user credentials. A proxy is not required or used.

**Why can I only see 18 products without an account?** That is the site's own guest limit. The actor keeps discovering products through the related-product graph on every product page and, when Cloudflare allows it for the run's IP, through the public product sitemap. `byUrl` resolves any product URL directly, even one outside the discovered set.

**Why are some revenue fields empty?** Many founders never publish revenue. Revenue above 10 trillion USD per month, zero and negative values are treated as invalid and omitted rather than emitted as fake data.

**Where does revenue history come from?** From the Stripe-backed chart embedded in the product page. Products that only report a single self-reported figure get `monthlyRevenue` and `revenueLabel`, not a fabricated history.

**Are groups supported?** No. Indie Hackers removed community groups; the old `/group/` pages return HTTP 410. Older inputs are handled without crashing and return a clear status message.

**What about old input names?** Saved tasks that still send `foundedDate-desc` or `memberCount-desc` as `sortBy` keep running: those values stay in the input schema and are mapped in code to the closest supported order. `mode=groups` is accepted, detected and explained in the run status. Legacy `urls`, `pageUrl` and `query` keys are mapped in code too.

**Why is the product order slightly different from the website?** `verified-revenue` reproduces the site's "Revenue: Verified First" order. `revenue-desc` sorts by the numeric revenue, so self-reported products can rank above a lower verified figure.

**Can I page through results?** Yes. Filter and sort first, then use `offset` with `maxItems`. For products the discovered pool is bounded (the guest directory plus related products and any accessible sitemap URLs), so a very large offset can return fewer rows.
